definition: Arizona Financial Text System (AZFinText) is a textual-based quantitative financial prediction system written by Robert P.
details: Schumaker of University of Texas at Tyler and Hsinchun Chen of the University of Arizona.

explainer.lead: AZFinText, short for Arizona Financial Text System, is a system for making quantitative financial predictions from text. Its central idea is that wording in financial documents can become useful input for numerical forecasts.

tiers.eli5: Imagine reading notes about a company and using clues in the words to make a numbered guess about its financial future. AZFinText is a computer system built around that idea, turning financial writing into predictions.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer would treat AZFinText as a text-to-forecast pipeline: prepare financial documents, derive features from their language, and produce quantitative predictions. The feature extractor, predictor, and forecast target are not fixed by the system’s high-level description. Predictions should be evaluated against later outcomes rather than treated as guaranteed financial results.
tiers.paperLevel: At a high level, AZFinText applies a mapping f: T -> y-hat, where T is financial text and y-hat is a quantitative financial prediction. It was written by Robert P. Schumaker of the University of Texas at Tyler and Hsinchun Chen of the University of Arizona. This definition does not imply a particular estimator, target variable, or performance guarantee.

explainer.example: A company releases an earnings announcement. AZFinText processes information from the announcement’s text and produces a numerical financial forecast related to the company.

usedIn.name: Quantitative financial prediction
usedIn.detail: Uses financial text as input to numerical forecasting.

usedIn.name: Financial text analysis
usedIn.detail: Connects the language of financial documents with predictive analysis.

explainer.intuition: Financial writing may contain clues that are difficult to represent as ordinary numbers. AZFinText’s idea is to extract predictive information from that language and use it in a quantitative forecast.
howItWorks: Start with text relevant to a financial prediction task.
Represent information in the wording in a form a predictor can use.
Apply the quantitative prediction system to that representation.
explainer.whyItMatters: It connects textual analysis with quantitative finance, allowing written financial information to inform forecasts rather than relying only on already-numerical data.
misconceptions: AZFinText is a financial prediction system, not a general-purpose conversational assistant.
A text-based forecast is an estimate, not a guarantee of financial performance.
